newsitem.title: INDIA: Panel to study fall in India crude oil production.
newsitem.headline: Panel to study fall in India crude oil production.

text.p: A five-member panel of experts will analyse why India's crude oil output is falling in 1996/97 (April-March), particularly in the western offshore fields, a petroleum ministry statement said on Monday.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said last week India's oil output in 1996/97 (April-March) was expected to dip to 32 million tonnes (around 640,000 barrels per day) against an earlier estimate of 33.7 million tonnes (674,000 bpd).
He said the estimate for the oil import bill for the same period had also risen to $9 billion from the earlier estimate of $7.8 billion, following the hardening of world crude prices.
Junior Petroleum Minister T.R.Baalu said on Wednesday crude oil output had declined due to the unexpected behaviour of the oil wells and a very high gas-oil ratio.
Gas in the wells had increased beyond the normal level, Baalu said, and added that separating gas from oil was not yielding the desired results.
The panel will suggest both short- and long-term measures to restore the reservoir health of the Western offshore fields and raise crude oil output in other parts of the country.

It will identify the technological problems affecting the exploitation of the western offshore fields and examine the need for strategic alliances with international oil companies for modern technology, the statement said.

The panel, to be headed by a geologist, K. Narayanan, will examine to what extent the recommendations of a previous committee on the Bombay High fields were implemented by the state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corp.
The committee will submit its report in three months.
